45	  // success. Each has exactly one representative in DIDS below.
46	  type DidShape =
47	    | ValidDidKey          // every check passes — public_key() returns the raw key bytes
48	    | WrongPrefixOrType     // not isinstance(str) or not did.startswith("did:key:") (didkey.py:57)
49	    | WrongMultibaseShape   // len(mb) != 48 or not mb.startswith("z") (didkey.py:60)
50	    | NotBase58Chars        // a character outside the base58btc alphabet (didkey.py:49-50)
51	    | WrongDecodedShape     // decoded length != 34, or wrong multicodec prefix (didkey.py:66)
52	
53	  // The signature-encoding regex (didkey.py:97-98): exactly 86 base64url characters.
54	  type SigShape = ValidSigEncoding | BadSigEncoding
55	
56	  // Whether a well-formed-looking signature is genuinely `did`'s Ed25519 signature over
57	  // the exact message presented — undecidable from any other field in this model, by
58	  // design (see header comment).
59	  type SigAuthenticity = Genuine | Forged
60	
61	  // _signer's own check (app.py:1157-1158): NONCE_RE = [0-9]{1,19}.
62	  type NonceShape = ValidNonceShape | BadNonceShape
63	
64	  type VerifyOutcome = VerifyAccepted | VerifyDidError | VerifySignatureError
65	  type SignerOutcome = SignerAccepted | SignerNonceRejected | SignerDidRejected | SignerSignatureRejected
66	
67	  pure val DIDS: Set[str] = Set(
68	    "did:key:zAlice", "did:key:zBob",   // ValidDidKey
69	    "missing-prefix",                    // WrongPrefixOrType
70	    "did:key:zBadMultibaseLen",          // WrongMultibaseShape
71	    "did:key:zBadCharI0Ol",              // NotBase58Chars
72	    "did:key:zBadDecoded"                // WrongDecodedShape

74	
75	  pure val SIGS: Set[str] = Set("sigWellFormed", "sigBadEncoding")
76	  pure val SIG_AUTHS: Set[SigAuthenticity] = Set(Genuine, Forged)
77	  pure val MESSAGES: Set[str] = Set("msgA", "msgB")
78	  // 1-19 digits (valid, including the 19-digit boundary) vs empty/non-digit/negative (bad).
79	  pure val NONCES: Set[str] = Set("1", "999999999999999999", "", "12a3")

81	  // --------------------------------------------------------------------- pure functions

83	  pure def didShapeOf(did: str): DidShape =
84	    if (did == "did:key:zAlice" or did == "did:key:zBob") ValidDidKey
85	    else if (did == "missing-prefix") WrongPrefixOrType
86	    else if (did == "did:key:zBadMultibaseLen") WrongMultibaseShape
87	    else if (did == "did:key:zBadCharI0Ol") NotBase58Chars
88	    else if (did == "did:key:zBadDecoded") WrongDecodedShape

92	    if (sig == "sigBadEncoding") BadSigEncoding else ValidSigEncoding
93	
94	  pure def nonceShapeOf(nonce: str): NonceShape =
95	    if (nonce == "1" or nonce == "999999999999999999") ValidNonceShape else BadNonceShape
96	
97	  // public_key() succeeding is exactly "the DID has ValidDidKey shape" (didkey.py:55-68).
98	  pure def publicKeyOk(did: str): bool = didShapeOf(did) == ValidDidKey
99

101	  // (didkey.py:71-78) — the same check, wrapped.
102	  pure def isDidPure(value: str): bool = publicKeyOk(value)
103	
104	  // verify() (didkey.py:89-103): public_key(did) is called FIRST, so a bad DID always wins
105	  // over a bad signature; a bad signature ENCODING is also a DidError (didkey.py:97-98),
106	  // not a SignatureError — only a well-formed-everything signature that fails the actual
107	  // Ed25519 check reaches SignatureError.
108	  pure def verifyOutcome(did: str, sig: str, auth: SigAuthenticity): VerifyOutcome =
109	    if (didShapeOf(did) != ValidDidKey) VerifyDidError

112	    else VerifyAccepted
113	
114	  // _signer() (app.py:1147-1169): nonce shape is checked before verify() is even called.
115	  pure def signerOutcome(nonce: str, did: str, sig: str, auth: SigAuthenticity): SignerOutcome = {

119	    else if (v == VerifySignatureError) SignerSignatureRejected
120	    else SignerAccepted
121	  }
122	
123	  // --------------------------------------------------------------------- state
124	
125	  type VerifyCall = { outcome: VerifyOutcome, did: str, sig: str }
126	  type SignerCall = { outcome: SignerOutcome, nonce: str, did: str, identity: str }
127	  type IsDidCall = { value: str, result: bool }
128

135	  }
136

138

178	  action abbreviate(did: str): bool = all {

183	  // verify(did, signature, message) — didkey.py:89.
184	  action verify(did: str, sig: str, auth: SigAuthenticity, message: str): bool = all {

188	  // _signer(did, sig, nonce, canonical) — app.py:1147. The one caller of verify(); on

191	  action signer(nonce: str, did: str, sig: str, auth: SigAuthenticity, message: str): bool = {
192	    val outcome = signerOutcome(nonce, did, sig, auth)

194	      st' = { ...st, signerLast: Some({
195	          outcome: outcome,
196	          nonce: nonce,
197	          did: did,

200	    }
201	  }

203	  action step = any {
204	    { nondet did = DIDS.oneOf()
205	      // Not a singleton: kept independently falsifiable (both true/false reachable

211

215	
216	    { nondet did = DIDS.oneOf()

218	
219	    { nondet did = DIDS.oneOf()

234	
235	  /// A malformed did:key or a malformed signature encoding is always reported as the

247	
248	  /// On a successful signed write, the identity `_signer` returns is exactly the did:key

257	
258	  /// is_did() and public_key() never disagree about which strings are valid did:keys —
259	  /// is_did is documented as exactly the same shape check public_key performs, just

261	  /// is_did() cannot be let through on a DID public_key() would then reject.
262	  val is_did_agrees_with_public_key: bool =
263	    match st.isDidLast {
264	      | Some(call) => call.result == (didShapeOf(call.value) == ValidDidKey)
265	      | None => true
266	    }
267	
268	  // --------------------------------------------------------------------- observations
269	
270	  /// public_key() successfully parsed a well-formed did:key into raw key bytes.
271	  val did_parsed_ok: bool =
272	    match st.publicKeyLast { | Some(shape) => shape == ValidDidKey | None => false }
273	
274	  /// public_key() rejected a malformed did:key (any of the four DidError categories).
275	  val did_parse_rejected: bool =
276	    match st.publicKeyLast { | Some(shape) => shape != ValidDidKey | None => false }
277	
278	  /// verify() accepted a (did, signature, message) triple end to end.
279	  val verify_accepted: bool =
280	    match st.verifyLast { | Some(call) => call.outcome == VerifyAccepted | None => false }
281	
282	  /// verify() rejected because the DID or the signature encoding was malformed (the
283	  /// 400-class refusal).
284	  val verify_did_error: bool =
285	    match st.verifyLast { | Some(call) => call.outcome == VerifyDidError | None => false }
286	
287	  /// verify() rejected a well-formed DID and encoding whose signature does not actually
288	  /// check out (the 403-class refusal).
289	  val verify_signature_error: bool =
290	    match st.verifyLast { | Some(call) => call.outcome == VerifySignatureError | None => false }
291	
292	  /// abbreviate() ran on an already-verified did:key, as its (unenforced) contract requires.
293	  val abbreviate_ran_on_valid_did: bool =
294	    st.abbreviateLast != None
295	
296	  /// _signer() accepted a full signed write end to end (nonce shape + verify()).
297	  val signer_accepted: bool =
298	    match st.signerLast { | Some(call) => call.outcome == SignerAccepted | None => false }
299	
300	  /// _signer() rejected a write before even checking the signature, because the nonce
301	  /// itself was not 1-19 digits.
302	  val signer_rejected_bad_nonce: bool =
303	    match st.signerLast { | Some(call) => call.outcome == SignerNonceRejected | None => false }

309	  /// _signer() rejected a write whose signature did not check out (propagated from verify()).
310	  val signer_rejected_signature: bool =
311	    match st.signerLast { | Some(call) => call.outcome == SignerSignatureRejected | None => false }
